paper.title: Online Sign Identification: Minimization of the Number of Errors in Thresholding Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Fixed-budget thresholding bandit, weighted number of errors
unmapped: Objective is the expected weighted number of misclassified arms sum_k a_k 1{hat s_k != s_k} (not the probability of any error)
the learner knows the per-arm error costs a_k and the threshold theta
settings.definition_quote: The distribution $\nu_k$ is supposed $\sigma$-sub-Gaussian ... The total number of rounds (and samples) $T$ is known in advance ... The objective is to minimize the expected weighted number of missclassified arms, where a mistake on arm $k$ has a known cost $a_k>0$, L_T = \sum_{k=1}^K a_k \mathbb{I}\{\hat{s}_k \ne s_k\}

settings.name_in_paper: Thresholding bandit, weighted number of errors, Gaussian instances (lower bound)
unmapped: Objective is the expected weighted number of misclassified arms sum_k a_k E_k
the learner knows the costs a_k and the gap magnitudes; only the signs are unknown
settings.definition_quote: for any algorithm and time horizon $T \geq K$, there exists an instance in which all arms $k \in [K]$ have Gaussian distributions with variance $\sigma^2$ and mean in $\{\Delta_k, -\Delta_k\}$

settings.name_in_paper: Thresholding bandit, one-parameter exponential family (lower bound)
unmapped: Objective is the expected weighted number of misclassified arms sum_k a_k E_k
each arm's mean is one of two known values mu_k < theta < tilde mu_k
settings.definition_quote: For each arm $k \in [K]$, we define two values $\mu_k, \tilde{\mu}_k \in \mathbb{R}$, with $\mu_k < \theta < \tilde{\mu}_k$. ... For some fixed one-parameter exponential family

unmapped: Objective is the expected sum of normalized gaps of misclassified arms, sum_k Delta_k E_k
the learner knows the threshold theta
settings.definition_quote: We show that our method applies for the sum-of-gaps objective $\sum_{k = 1}^K \Delta_k E_k$. This is not a particular case of the setting discussed previously since $a_k$ was known to the algorithm, while $\Delta_k$ is unknown.

algorithms.name: Index-based algorithm for thresholding bandit (Algorithm 1, generic F satisfying Assumption 1)

symbols.Opt_4: min over allocations N with sum_k N_k = T of sum_k a_k exp(-4 N_k Delta_k^2)
symbols.a_k: known cost of an error on arm k

conditions: worst case over instances with Gaussian arms of variance sigma^2 and means in {Delta_k, -Delta_k}

source.label: thm:lower_bound_tao
source.quote: Let $\left(\Delta_{1}, \ldots, \Delta_{K}\right)$ be a sequence of gaps. Then for any algorithm and time horizon $T \geq K$, there exists an instance in which all arms $k \in [K]$ have Gaussian distributions with variance $\sigma^2$ and mean in $\{\Delta_k, -\Delta_k\}$ such that \mathbb{E}[L_T] \ge \frac{1}{4} \min_{\sum_k N_k = T} \sum_{k=1}^K a_k e^{- 4 N_k \Delta_k^2}

results.notes: Stated as 'similar to Theorem 20 in Tao et al. 2019' but re-derived with weights a_k; treated as new. Quantity is expected weighted number of errors (no vocabulary term).

symbols.Opt_KL: min over allocations N with sum_k N_k = T of sum_k a_k exp(-N_k max{KL(mu_k, tilde mu_k), KL(tilde mu_k, mu_k)})
symbols.a_k: known cost of an error on arm k

conditions: supremum over the 2^K instances mu_S obtained by flipping each arm's mean between mu_k and tilde mu_k

source.label: th:lb on flips
source.quote: For any algorithm, \sup_{S \in \mathcal P([K])} \mathbb{E}[L_T(\mu_S)] \ge \frac{1}{4} \min_{N:\sum_k N_k = T} \sum_{k=1}^K a_k \exp \left( - N_k \max\{\KL(\mu_k, \tilde{\mu}_k),\KL(\tilde{\mu}_k, \mu_k)\} \right)

results.notes: General exponential-family version; its Gaussian special case equals Theorem 1 (r1).

symbols.c_0: constant in the exponent of the assumed loss guarantee
symbols.c_1: multiplicative constant of the assumed loss guarantee
symbols.K_0: number of arms with mean +/- epsilon
symbols.eps_0: small mean epsilon of the K_0 arms near the threshold

conditions: algorithms satisfying E[L_T] <= c_1 min_{sum N_k = T} sum_k exp(-c_0 N_k Delta_k^2) on mu'_+ and mu'_-
mu_{K_0+1} large enough that the oracle pulls all arms on mu'_+
max over the instances mu_{+eps}, mu_{-eps}

source.quote: If $\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{\tilde{\mu}}[L_T] \le c_1 \min_{\sum_k N_k = T} \sum_k e^{-c_0 N_k \Delta_k^2}$ for constants $c_0, c_1$ on $\tilde{\mu} \in \{\mu'_+, \mu'_-\}$, then \max_{\mu \in \{\mu_{+ \varepsilon}, \mu_{- \varepsilon}\}}\mathbb{E}_\mu\left[\sum_{k=1}^{K_0} N_{k,T} \right] \ge \frac{1}{2(\mu_{K_0+1}-\varepsilon)^2} \left(c_0 \frac{T + H^{\log}}{H} + \log \frac{K_0}{32 c_1 H} \right)

results.notes: Lower bound on the expected number of pulls of near-threshold arms (not on the loss); restated as Lemma 2 in the appendix.

bound.expression_latex: \sum_{k=1}^K a_k \left(e\cdot \exp\left(- \frac{ \frac{1}{2}\left(T-\sum_{j \notin S_k} t_{j,0}(C_k)\right)- \sum_{j \in S_k} t_j(C_k)}{\sum_{j \in S_k} 1/\Delta_j^2}\right)+ T \cdot e^{- t_{k}(C_k) \Delta_k^2}\right)

symbols.a_k: known cost of an error on arm k
symbols.Tsum_k: sum_{j in S_k} t_j(C_k), with t_j(C) solving F(t, t Delta_j^2; a_j) = C
symbols.t_k: t_k(C_k), solution of F(t, t Delta_k^2; a_k) = C_k

conditions: index function F satisfies Assumption 1 (non-decreasing in n and x, F(n, ny; a) -> infinity)
for i not in S_k, the index of arm i reaches C_k within t_{i,0}(C_k) pulls almost surely
tuning: free choice of thresholds C_1,...,C_K and sets S_k

source.label: thm:expected_errors_bound
source.quote: Let $K \geq 1$, $a_1,\dots,a_K >0$, $T\geq 1$, and $\sigma >0$. Let $F$ that satisfies Assumption~\ref{ass:index_shape}. Let $C_1,\ldots, C_K > \max_k F(0,0; a_k)$. ... Then the expected loss of Algorithm~\ref{alg:index-based} is upper-bounded as \mathbb{E}[L_T^{\mathbb{A}}] \le \sum_{k=1}^K a_k \left(e\cdot \exp\left(- \frac{ \frac{1}{2}\left(T-\sum_{j \notin S_k} t_{j,0}(C_k)\right)- \sum_{j \in S_k} t_j(C_k)}{\sum_{j \in S_k} 1/\Delta_j^2}\right)+ T \cdot e^{- t_{k}(C_k) \Delta_k^2}\right)

results.notes: Generic bound for all index-based algorithms; applied to LSA in the appendix (Eq. upper_bound_LSA) with t_j(C)=W(e^C Delta_j^2)/Delta_j^2, which is not separately recorded.

symbols.H_thr: sum over all arms j of 1/Delta_j^2, with Delta_j = |mu_j - theta|/sqrt(2 sigma^2)

conditions: unit costs a_k = 1 for all k

source.label: cor:APT_upperbound
source.quote: Suppose that for all $k \in [K]$, $a_k = 1$. For all $T\in \mathbb{N}^*$, \mathbb{E}[L_T^{\text{APT}}] \le 2 K\sqrt{e\cdot T} \cdot \exp \left( - \frac{1}{4}\frac{T}{\sum_{j = 1}^K 1/\Delta_j^2} \right)

results.notes: Bound on expected number of errors for APT variant returning signs at t_max; also bounds the zero-one loss (probability of any error).

bound.expression: A_out + E*sum_Sp(a_k*exp(-((T - A_S)/2 + G_S)/H_S + C_0)) + T*sum_Sp(a_k*exp(-C_0 + log(1/(a_k*Delta_k**2))))
bound.expression_latex: \sum_{k\notin S'} a_k + e \sum_{k\in S'} a_k \exp\left(- \frac{\frac{1}{2}(T - \sum_{j \notin S} a_j e^{C-1}) + \sum_{j \in S} \frac{1}{\Delta_j^2}\log \frac{1}{a_j\Delta_j^2}}{\sum_{j \in S} 1/\Delta_j^2} + C \right) + T \sum_{k\in S'} a_k \exp \left( - C + \log (1/(a_k\Delta_k^2)) \right)

symbols.sum_Sp: sum over arms k in S'
symbols.A_S: sum_{j not in S} a_j e^{C-1}
symbols.C_0: the free constant C of the corollary
symbols.a_k: known cost of an error on arm k

conditions: S' subset of S subset of [K]
C >= 1 + max_{k in S} log(1/(a_k Delta_k^2))
tuning: free analysis choice of S, S', C

source.label: cor:FWTupperbound
source.quote: Let $S, S'$ be two sets with $S' \subseteq S \subseteq [K]$ and let $C \in \mathbb{R}$ be such that $C \ge 1 + \max\limits_{k \in S} \log \frac{1}{a_k \Delta_k^2}$. Then, for all $T\ge 1$ \mathbb{E}[L_T^{\text{FWT}}] \le \sum_{k\notin S'} a_k + e \sum_{k\in S'} a_k \exp(...) + T \sum_{k\in S'} a_k \exp \left( - C + \log (1/(a_k\Delta_k^2)) \right)

results.notes: The text also states (Eq. large_T_bound_FWT, not a formal statement) that for large T, E[L_T^FWT] <= 2 sqrt(eT) sum_k a_k exp(-(1/4)(T + 2 sum_j (1/Delta_j^2) log(a_k Delta_k^2/(a_j Delta_j^2)))/sum_j 1/Delta_j^2), within factor 1/4 in the exponent of the non-adaptive oracle.

bound.regime: T >= 2 sum_j (1/Delta_j^2)(3 + 3 log(Delta_j max_i Delta_i/(min_i Delta_i)^2) - log(T/e))

symbols.H_thr: sum over all arms j of 1/Delta_j^2

conditions: T >= 2 sum_j (1/Delta_j^2)(3 + 3 log(Delta_j max_i Delta_i/(min_i Delta_i)^2) - log(T/e))
tuning: FWT index F(n,x) = x' - (3/2) log x' + (3/2) log n with x' = max(x, 3/2)

source.quote: In the regime where $T\ge 2 \sum_{j=1}^k \frac{1}{\Delta_j^2}\left(3 + 3 \log\frac{\Delta_j \max_{i}\Delta_i}{(\min_{i}\Delta_i)^2}-\log\frac{T}{e}\right)$, we show that \mathbb{E}[\sum_{k = 1}^K \Delta_k E_k] \le 2 \sqrt{e T} \sum_{k} \Delta_k \exp\left(- \frac{1}{2}\frac{\frac{T}{2} + \sum_{j} \frac{3}{2}\frac{1}{\Delta_j^2}\log \frac{\Delta_k^2}{\Delta_j^2}}{\sum_{j} 1/\Delta_j^2}\right).

results.notes: Sum-of-gaps loss; FWT variant with a modified index (3/2 factors).
